description: Consistency cross-check across all five Sprint 4 Phase 6/7/1.5 artifacts (docs/phase-7-routing/sprint4_ar0_routing_index.json, sprint4_ar1_assignments.json, sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json, sprint4_implementation_execution_plan.json, sprint4-ar5-rs-computation.md), mirroring docs/phase-8-alignment/sprint3_ir1_agent_flags.json's real structure and role exactly: every agent named across the bundle re-confirmed real via a fresh glob/directory check (not trusted on the bundle's own say-so), every assignment internally consistent, and no contradiction between AR.0/AR.1/AR.3/execution-plan/AR.5.
reviewer_note: Runtime persona for this pass was computed by the Phase 8 harness as product-manager-agent (claude-global-library/agents/product-manager-agent/agent.md, version 1.0.0, read in full together with its 3 mandatory skills: product-management-core, product-analytics-core, user-story-mapping-core). Unlike Sprint 2/3's IR.1 passes (reliability-auditor, then consensus-agent -- both flagged by their own reviewer_notes as a domain/persona mismatch for this kind of routing-artifact citation cross-check), this dispatch has a different and arguably sharper defect: product-manager-agent is not merely domain-adjacent, it is the SAME agent identity that authored every one of the five Sprint 4 bundle files under review here (each file's own "author" field reads "product-manager-agent"). An IR.1 alignment check performed by the artifacts' own author is a self-review, not an independent second pass -- the same structural concern this project's own p1_security_override maker-checker principle exists to prevent for code review, applied here to documentation review. This is disclosed as a Phase 8 agent-selection-step observation, not silently worked around: the verification work below was still performed to the letter of the task instructions (fresh agent-existence glob, independent GitHub-issue re-fetch via mcp__github-api__github_get_issue, independent recount of every numeric claim from the real JSON/markdown content, not accepted on any artifact's own prose), using product-management-core/product-analytics-core's own emphasis on evidence-based verification (never trust a metric without recomputing it) as the closest applicable general method from the loaded skill set, since none of its domain-specific formulas (WSJF, A/B power, Kano, NPV-IRR, BG/NBD, Shapley) apply to a documentation/JSON cross-check. Every numeric claim below was independently recomputed by directly reading the real files, not estimated or taken on any artifact's own say-so.
method: For Sprint 4's single candidate item (DASH-STORY-026 / FR-013 / GitHub #23): (1) read sprint4_ar0_routing_index.json's candidate_items, agent_existence_verification, scoring_model, and advisory_review_roster blocks in full; (2) read sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's assignments[0] (DASH-STORY-026 and its three sub-tasks DEV/QA/REVIEW), p1_security_override, dependency_integrity_check, routing_gaps, and summary blocks in full; (3) read sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json's three context_windows[] entries and summary block in full, cross-checking each sub_task_id/assigned_agent/context_budget_tokens triple against sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's own assignment; (4) read sprint4_implementation_execution_plan.json's scope_note, sequencing_note, file_collision_analysis, retry_policy, all three prompts[0].sub_tasks[] blocks, execution_summary, and determinism_guardrail in full, confirming its 1-story/3-prompt shape and dependency chain (Dev->QA->Review) matches sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's own dependency_integrity_check.sprint_4_edges with no story added or dropped; (5) read sprint4-ar5-rs-computation.md in full and independently re-verified its own numeric claims against the real JSON content using direct recount rather than accepting its prose: the score_range {min, max, mean} in sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's summary recomputed from the three assigned sub-task scores (0.900, 0.825, 0.800); the '9 acceptance-criteria entries' figure recomputed by counting AC-026-DEV-1/2/3 + AC-026-QA-1/2/3 + AC-026-REVIEW-1/2/3 in sprint4_ar1_assignments.json; the '26 context-window source-citation entries (12+7+7)' figure recomputed by counting every files_to_read_or_modify + domain_files_cited_across_review_rounds + github_issues + cross_reference entry in each of sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json's three context_windows[] blocks; the rule-of-three floors (0.67 at n=9, 0.89 at n=26) recomputed from those same counts; (6) fetched GitHub issues #23 and #25 fresh via mcp__github-api__github_get_issue (not read from any bundle file's paraphrase) to independently confirm their title, state, label, and body text match every bundle file's citation of them; (7) re-verified every one of the 6 distinct agent names (python-backend-engineer, integration-testing-engineer, qa-testing-agent, api-security-auditor, solution-architect, consensus-agent) and all 7 distinct skill names cited in the IEP's ---persona--- headers (fastapi-core, api-design-core, error-handling-patterns, integration-testing-core, contract-testing-core, api-testing-core, application-security-core) actually exist on disk via a fresh `test -f` check against claude-global-library/agents/{name}/agent.md and skills/{name}/SKILL.md, not trusted on sprint4_ar0_routing_index.json's own agent_existence_verification claim; (8) grepped the entire docs/phase-7-routing/ directory and the design doc itself for the string 'Check 4b' and 'Phase C' to test sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json's own claim that a 'consensus-agent's Phase C gate review (Check 4b)' flagged a specific context-window gap.

per_item_cross_check.verdict: MATCH ON SCORES/BUDGETS/DEPENDENCIES, WITH ONE UNRESOLVED RESIDUAL DEFECT - see flags_raised IR1-S4-F1
per_item_cross_check.detail: sprint4_ar0_routing_index.json SPRINT4-CAND-001 (split into sub-tasks -A implementer, -B test-author, plus a 3-person advisory_review_roster) maps 1:1 onto sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's single story DASH-STORY-026, itself split into three sub-tasks DEV/QA/REVIEW that fold AR.0's implementer split and its separate advisory roster into one story, exactly as sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's own structural_note discloses (not silently reshaped). All three sub-task scores carry forward byte-for-byte from AR.0 into AR.1: python-backend-engineer 0.900 (domain_match 0.90, skill_coverage 0.90), integration-testing-engineer 0.825 (0.85/0.80), api-security-auditor 0.800 (0.85/0.75) -- independently re-verified by direct arithmetic (0.5*0.90+0.5*0.90=0.900; 0.5*0.85+0.5*0.80=0.825; 0.5*0.85+0.5*0.75=0.800), all correct. qa-testing-agent (0.725), solution-architect (0.725), and consensus-agent (0.725) are also carried forward unchanged and consistently marked above_threshold=true against AR.0's own 0.70 scoring threshold and above_threshold=false against AR.1's own 0.75 assignment threshold in both files -- the two different thresholds for two different decisions (AR.0 scores fit, AR.1 decides who is assigned) are consistently applied, not conflated. GitHub #23 and #25 were independently re-fetched (not read from any bundle file's paraphrase) and match every bundle file's citation of their title, state ('open'), label ('not-implemented' for #23, 'bug' for #25), and body content word-for-word against the routing files' own quoted excerpts -- no fabricated or drifted GitHub citation found. All 6 agent names and all 7 skill names cited across the bundle's ---persona--- headers and evidence fields were independently re-confirmed to exist on disk by this pass's own fresh file check, not trusted on sprint4_ar0_routing_index.json's own agent_existence_verification claim (which itself already disclosed, honestly, that its recursive Glob search timed out twice and it fell back to `ls -d` -- this pass's own check used a different, simpler method (`test -f` per name) and got the same 6-for-6 result, corroborating rather than merely repeating that claim). context_budget_tokens (7000/5500/5000, summing to 17500) is identical between AR.3's context_windows[] and the IEP's own 'Context Budget: N tokens' line in all three dispatch-ready prompts. dependency_integrity_check.sprint_4_edges (DEV:[], QA:[DEV], REVIEW:[DEV,QA]) matches the IEP's own depends_on fields and sequencing_note exactly, and its file_collision_analysis.collision_finding of NONE is independently correct: the three production files (openapi.yaml, schemas.py, app.py) are Dev-owned-write/others-read-only, the new test file is QA-owned-write/others-read-only, and Review modifies no source file at all -- no two sub-tasks claim write access to the same file, and the strict sequential ordering means no concurrent-write window could occur even if they had. However, sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json's own DEV context window contains one unverifiable, unsupported provenance claim about a document that does not exist anywhere in this bundle or this repo -- see IR1-S4-F1.

dependency_and_reference_integrity_check.verdict: MATCH - no orphaned reference, no missing sub-task, no cycle
dependency_and_reference_integrity_check.detail: Sprint 4's one story (DASH-STORY-026) and its three sub-tasks (DEV, QA, REVIEW) appear consistently across all four JSON artifacts with matching assigned_agent, score, and context_budget_tokens in every place they are repeated (AR.1's own sub_tasks[] fields, AR.3's context_windows[], the IEP's own prompts[0].sub_tasks[] blocks). dependency_integrity_check.sprint_4_edges was independently re-traversed: DEV has no dependency, QA depends on DEV, REVIEW depends on both DEV and QA -- a strict linear chain, matching the IEP's own depends_on arrays and sequencing_note exactly, and matching sprint4-ar5-rs-computation.md's own restatement of the same three-edge structure. No Sprint 4 sub-task is referenced by any Sprint 1-3 story's own depends_on array (this file's own logging_note states Sprint 4 'Depends on nothing else in Sprint 4'), and no cycle exists in the combined 4-sprint graph. GitHub #23 is referenced consistently (never renumbered, never paraphrased into a different claim) as the issue this story closes across all five bundle files; GitHub #25 is referenced consistently across AR.3/IEP/AR.5 (AR.0/AR.1 do not need to cite it directly, since it is a negative-scope boundary discovered during AR.3's context design, not part of the routing/scoring decision itself) as a named, explicitly-not-fixed adjacent defect -- never silently dropped from later files once disclosed in AR.3.

rs_computation_cross_check.verdict: COMPUTATION ARITHMETIC CORRECT AND HONESTLY SCOPED - no defect found in AR.5 itself
rs_computation_cross_check.detail: sprint4-ar5-rs-computation.md's own arithmetic, RS = sqrt(a x b) = sqrt(1.00 x 1.00) = 1.00, is correct arithmetic given its stated inputs, and this pass independently re-derived both inputs rather than accepting them on the document's own say-so: 'a' (citation/consistency self-check) checked out clean against this pass's own independent recount above (scores, context budgets, FR/GitHub-issue references all consistent across all four routing files); 'b' (atomic-fact self-check) also checked out clean (the design doc's status line, the dependency_integrity_check/depends_on match, and the file_collision_analysis.collision_finding of NONE were all independently re-confirmed by this pass, not merely re-read). Unlike Sprint 2/3, this document is unusually forthright about its own weaker evidentiary basis: it explicitly discloses that no sprint4-phase-c-gate-results.md exists, that its 'a'/'b' are a single-reviewer self-check rather than a paired-detector (C-1 NLI/FactScore + C-2 RAGAS) census, and recommends a dedicated Sprint 4 Phase C gate pass before Phase B dispatch rather than silently presenting RS=1.00 as equivalent in evidentiary weight to Sprint 2/3's paired-detector-backed RS=1.00. This pass independently re-verified the two numeric units the document's own rule-of-three side-computation depends on: the '9 acceptance-criteria entries' figure (AC-026-DEV-1/2/3 + AC-026-QA-1/2/3 + AC-026-REVIEW-1/2/3, counted directly from sprint4_ar1_assignments.json = 9, matches) and the '26 context-window source-citation entries (12 for DEV + 7 for QA + 7 for REVIEW)' figure (independently recounted from sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json's own three context_windows[] blocks: DEV = 4 files_to_read_or_modify + 5 domain_files_cited_across_review_rounds + 2 github_issues + 1 cross_reference = 12; QA = 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 7; REVIEW = 3 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 7; total 12+7+7=26, matches exactly). The rule-of-three floors (0.67 at n=9, 0.89 at n=26) are also arithmetically correct: 3/9=0.333 -> sqrt(0.667x0.667)=0.667; 3/26~=0.115 -> sqrt(0.885x0.885)=0.885. No defect found in AR.5's own computation or disclosure -- it is, on this pass's independent re-check, the most self-critical of the four Phase-7-scoped RS documents produced so far in this engagement, not the least.

flags_raised.detail: sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json's DASH-STORY-026-DEV context window includes src/dashanan/domain/entity_record.py in its files_to_read_or_modify list, with the stated reason: 'Flagged as missing from this context window by consensus-agent's Phase C gate review (Check 4b) -- the one construction detail the design doc pushed onto the implementer was also the one file this window omitted; added here so the Dev sub-task is not instructed to read a file outside its own declared context-budget source list.' This pass independently checked whether that stated provenance is real. It is not, on the evidence available in this repo: (a) sprint4-ar5-rs-computation.md, the same engagement's own Sprint 4 evidentiary-gap disclosure, states explicitly and unambiguously that 'No sprint4-phase-c-gate-results.md exists in this repo' and that Sprint 4's a/b inputs are 'this session's own single-reviewer citation/consistency check... not a two-detector census' -- i.e., no Phase C gate process (consensus-agent-run or otherwise) is recorded anywhere as having executed against the Sprint 4 bundle; (b) a fresh grep of the entire docs/phase-7-routing/ directory and the design doc itself for the literal string 'Check 4b' returns exactly one hit -- the sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json line quoted above -- with no corresponding gate-results document, checklist, or prior-round citation anywhere else in the repo that defines what 'Check 4b' is or records its output; (c) sprint4_ar0_routing_index.json and sprint4_ar1_assignments.json, both of which would be the natural place to record a Phase C finding that changed a context-window file list, make no mention of any such review or finding. The underlying SUBSTANCE of the addition is not in dispute and is independently well-grounded: the design doc's own Section 4.2 step 3 (fr013-predicate-schema-design.md:200, confirmed by this pass's own direct read) does explicitly defer the EntityAttributeRecord construction detail to entity_record.py's own constructor, so citing that file in the DEV context window is a correct and useful addition on its merits. The defect is narrower and specifically about PROVENANCE: sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json attributes that correct addition to a specific, named review mechanism and checklist item ('consensus-agent's Phase C gate review (Check 4b)') that this pass could not find any supporting evidence for anywhere in the bundle or the wider repo, and that a sibling document in the same bundle (AR.5) explicitly states did not occur for Sprint 4. A reviewing agent or future auditor who trusted this citation would believe a Phase C gate document exists and ran a 'Check 4b' against Sprint 4, when the same engagement's own AR.5 says plainly that it did not.
flags_raised.resolution: NOT FIXED by this pass -- flagged for disclosure rather than silently edited, consistent with sprint3_ir1_agent_flags.json's own precedent of disclosing rather than unilaterally rewriting another artifact's prose outside this file's own scope. Recommended fix for whoever owns the next Phase 7 documentation-correction pass: either (a) run the actual dedicated Sprint 4 Phase C gate pass AR.5 itself already recommends and record it as sprint4-phase-c-gate-results.md, at which point this citation would become true and verifiable, or (b) if no such gate ever ran, correct sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json's DASH-STORY-026-DEV entity_record.py 'why' field to state plainly that this pass (or whichever pass actually added it) added the file directly from the design doc's own Section 4.2 step 3 deferral, without inventing an intermediate review-mechanism citation.

flags_list: DASH-STORY-026-DEV (sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json entity_record.py citation), UNSUPPORTED_PROCESS_PROVENANCE_CITATION, MEDIUM, NOT FIXED (disclosed, outside this pass's edit authority for a sibling artifact's prose)
not_flagged_but_disclosed: Phase 8 harness dispatched this review under the product-manager-agent persona/skill set, the same agent identity that authored all five Sprint 4 bundle files under review; see reviewer_note above for why this is a self-review concern distinct from (and in one sense sharper than) the domain-mismatch concern sprint2_ir1_agent_flags.json (reliability-auditor) and sprint3_ir1_agent_flags.json (consensus-agent) both already raised for their own Sprint 2/3 IR.1 passes. This is a Phase 8 agent-selection-step observation for whoever owns that routing rule, not a defect in the Sprint 4 artifacts under review.

sprint4_ar0_routing_index.json's reduced 2-signal scoring model (domain_match/skill_coverage only, 0.70 threshold) versus sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's re-application of the fuller 0.75 assignment threshold to the same underlying scores is a disclosed, deliberate methodology reuse from Sprint 3, documented in both files' own methodology_reuse_note/threshold_source fields -- not re-litigated here since both files already disclose and justify it, and this pass independently confirmed the two thresholds are applied consistently rather than conflated anywhere in the bundle.

sprint4_implementation_execution_plan.json's word_count_band_note discloses that all three Sprint 4 prompts (741/668/712 words) exceed the reused 400-600-word band; this is explicitly disclosed as intentional (binding AC/must-not-deviate text and file:line citations are not compressed to fit a target band) in that file's own text and is not treated as a defect by this pass, consistent with the same disclosed-overage posture sprint3_ir1_agent_flags.json's own not_flagged_but_disclosed section already accepted for Sprint 3's prompts.

sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's own p1_security_override.considered_and_not_triggered analysis for DASH-STORY-026 was independently re-checked against its own three literal criteria (Zone 7 storage touch, ZoneRepository port touch, cross-tenant isolation touch) and the design doc's own Section 4.2 text; the 'not triggered, non-blocking advisory review attached instead' conclusion is independently correct on this pass's own reading -- not re-litigated as a finding, only confirmed.
verdict: ALIGNED WITH ONE MEDIUM-SEVERITY DEFECT FOUND, NOT FIXED (outside this file's edit authority over a sibling artifact)
verdict_scope: ALIGNED here means citation/reference/arithmetic-alignment across all five Sprint 4 Phase 7/1.5 artifacts: the one story and its three sub-tasks' agent assignments, scores, and context budgets match everywhere they are repeated, no sub-task is orphaned or dropped between the routing index, assignments, context windows, and execution plan, the strict Dev->QA->Review dependency chain is consistent and cycle-free, every GitHub issue and design-doc citation independently re-verified matches the real source, and every named agent and skill independently re-confirmed to exist on disk. This pass found one MEDIUM-severity defect (IR1-S4-F1: an unsupported claim in sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json that a 'consensus-agent's Phase C gate review (Check 4b)' flagged a specific context-window gap, when this engagement's own AR.5 document explicitly states no Phase C gate artifact or process exists for Sprint 4) which is disclosed but not fixed, since editing another artifact's own prose is outside this file's stated scope (this IR.1 file records findings against the bundle, mirroring sprint3_ir1_agent_flags.json's own posture toward its one LOW-severity unfixed finding). This verdict does NOT itself certify Sprint 4 as execution-ready for Phase B dispatch -- see execution_readiness below, which considers the 2 still-OPEN decisions (SP4-DEC-201/202) sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's own summary.open_user_decisions already discloses and that this pass did not resolve (they are genuine user decisions, not alignment defects).
verdict_rationale: Every sub-task ID, agent assignment, score, context-budget figure, dependency edge, GitHub-issue citation, and named agent/skill cross-checked exactly across all five Sprint 4 artifacts, with every number independently recomputed from the real source content rather than accepted on any artifact's own prose (score arithmetic 0.5*domain_match+0.5*skill_coverage re-verified for all 6 candidates; the 9-AC and 26-source-citation counts re-verified by direct recount; both GitHub issues re-fetched fresh via the GitHub API, not read from a bundle paraphrase; all 6 agents and 7 skills re-confirmed to exist on disk via a fresh file check). One real defect was found by this independent checking rather than accepted on the bundle's own say-so: sprint4_ar3_context_windows.json cites a specific review mechanism and checklist item ('consensus-agent's Phase C gate review, Check 4b') as the source of one context-window addition, but no artifact anywhere in this bundle or repo records that review having run, and a sibling document in the same bundle (sprint4-ar5-rs-computation.md) explicitly states that no Phase C gate document or process exists for Sprint 4 at all (IR1-S4-F1, MEDIUM -- the underlying file addition is itself correct and well-grounded in the design doc, only its stated provenance is unsupported). This is disclosed rather than silently repeated or silently corrected without disclosure, consistent with this project's own established IR.1 practice across Sprints 2 and 3.

execution_readiness.determination: NOT YET EXECUTION-READY - two genuinely open user decisions remain, unrelated to this pass's one alignment finding.
execution_readiness.reasoning: sprint4_ar1_assignments.json's own summary.open_user_decisions lists 2 items (SP4-DEC-201, SP4-DEC-202), both still status OPEN at the time of this IR.1 pass: SP4-DEC-201 asks the user to authorize the non-blocking api-security-auditor advisory review attached to DASH-STORY-026-REVIEW; SP4-DEC-202 restates sprint4_ar0_routing_index.json's own SP4-DEC-001 team-shape question (one generalist QA owner vs. per-item testing specialist routing) and is explicitly a preference question, not a coverage gate. The IEP's own execution_summary.status field independently confirms the same posture: 'PREPARED, NOT EXECUTED -- open_user_decisions SP4-DEC-201... and SP4-DEC-202... remain OPEN... Still awaiting Phase 7 STOP 7 user review before any Phase B dispatch.' Separately, sprint4-ar5-rs-computation.md itself recommends running a dedicated Sprint 4 Phase C gate pass (producing a real sprint4-phase-c-gate-results.md) before Phase B dispatch, a recommendation this pass's own IR1-S4-F1 finding independently reinforces -- the one unsupported citation this pass found is precisely the kind of gap a real Phase C gate pass would either substantiate or correct, rather than leaving it as an isolated, unverifiable citation in one artifact.
blockers_for_phase_b_dispatch: SP4-DEC-201: authorization of the api-security-auditor advisory review on DASH-STORY-026-REVIEW - the IEP's own review_prompt is dispatch-ready but the story's own summary states the review 'must actually run and report before this story is presented as closing GitHub #23', and dispatch itself is gated on this authorization per the IEP's own execution_summary.status

SP4-DEC-202: team-shape preference (one generalist QA owner vs. per-item specialist) - explicitly non-blocking for dispatch per the IEP's own status field, but should be decided before this pattern repeats into a future sprint

Not a formally listed open_user_decision, but recommended by sprint4-ar5-rs-computation.md's own Verdict section and reinforced by this pass's IR1-S4-F1: running an actual Sprint 4 Phase C gate pass (producing sprint4-phase-c-gate-results.md) before Phase B dispatch, so Sprint 4 carries the same evidentiary standard as Sprint 2/3 and so citations like the one IR1-S4-F1 flags are either substantiated by a real gate artifact or corrected
